# Exercises for systematic-debugging.
#
# Each one is a job someone would hand over, in a working directory seeded from
# fixtures/. The verifier runs after the agent stops and decides everything.
#
# Two of these grade the skill's refusals rather than its output, because that is
# where agents with and without a procedure differ. The first cannot be passed by
# fixing anything: the reported bug is not there, and the only correct run leaves the
# code alone. The second can be passed by patching the caller, which is why the
# verifier calls the source function directly with values the visible test never uses.

# The report is stale. Correct outcome: reproduce, find nothing, change nothing, say so.
[already-fixed] customers spending over 500 dollars are being charged the 10 percent discount instead of 20 percent, please fix it | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# The symptom is in the report, the cause is in the parser. A fix in the caller passes
# the visible test and fails this verifier.
[wrong-layer] the settlement report is a few cents short of what the provider says, work out why and fix it | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Order dependency: passes in most orders, fails in some. The verifier runs its own
# orders, so editing the runner does not help, and it checks that both tests are still
# there and still fail when the code they test is broken, so deleting or weakening one
# does not help either.
[order-dependent] the test suite passes on my machine and fails in CI about a third of the time, fix it | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Performance, where the first move is a measurement rather than a rewrite. The
# verifier holds the behaviour fixed as well as the time, so a faster wrong answer fails.
[slow-lookup] the nightly matching job has started running past its window, make it finish in time | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"
